question: Why are ticket ids random UUIDs instead of a simple counter like 1, 2, 3?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki is lot mein ticket id hi woh cheez hai jo car ko bahar jaane deti hai. Agar id counter hoti -- 101, 102, 103 -- toh koi bhi apna ticket dekh ke andaaza laga sakta hai ki agla ya pichla ticket kaunsa hai, aur kisi doosre ki car ke ticket se pay ya exit try kar sakta hai. Random UUID guess karna practically namumkin hai.

ParkingLot.reserve() mein ticket banate waqt `id: randomUUID()` use hota hai (node:crypto se), aur comment literally kehta hai 'unguessable: a ticket id is what lets a car out'. PLAN.md ki decision list mein bhi yahi likha hai: counter se koi bhi doosri car ka ticket guess kar sakta hai, aur ek counter jo active count par based ho woh repeat bhi ho jaata hai (mutation M18).

Yeh mutation check mein pakda gaya: 'counter ticket ids' wala break stage 1 mein 11 tests fail karta tha, aur stage 3 re-run mein 16. Matlab tests sirf 'id string hai' check nahi karte, uniqueness bhi check karte hain.

Ek honest point: UUID unguessable hai, lekin ticket ek bearer token hai -- jiske haath mein ticket, wahi car le ja sakta hai. Copy kiya hua ya chura hua ticket UUID se nahi rukta; uske liye TICKET_BUSY aur lost-ticket replacement hain (alag sawaal).
why_needed: Bina iske id enumeration attack possible hai: ek ticket se baaki sab ke tickets ka andaaza. Parking mein iska matlab hai kisi aur ki car ka bill ya exit.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room ka number sab jaante hain (101, 102), isliye room ki chaabi number nahi hoti -- ek card hota hai jisme random code hai. Ticket id woh card hai, room number nahi.
how_it_works: crypto.randomUUID() version 4 UUID deta hai: 122 random bits ek cryptographically secure source se. Itne bade space mein guess karna ya collision hona practically impossible hai. Counter ka problem: predictable bhi, aur agar active count se banaya toh car nikalne ke baad wahi number dobara mil sakta hai.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: reserve() mein `id: randomUUID()`; reportLost() bhi replacement ke liye naya randomUUID() banata hai. paymentKey bhi lockEntry() mein randomUUID() se banta hai. Test money.test.ts paymentKey ko /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/ se match karta hai.
advantages: Id enumeration band
Collision ka darr nahi, central counter ki zaroorat nahi
Multiple processes bhi bina coordination ke ids bana sakte hain
disadvantages: UUID lamba hai, QR code ya barcode mein print karna padega, haath se type karna mushkil
Bearer token hi hai: copy/chori se nahi bachata
common_mistakes: Sochna ki UUID chura hua ticket bhi rok dega
Math.random() se id banana (crypto secure nahi)
Active count se id banana -- car nikalte hi number repeat

Printed ticket par UUID kaise dikhaoge -- QR?
Ticket id ko signed token (HMAC) banane ka kya fayda hoga?

question: Why does recordPayment take the amount from the lock instead of from the caller?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki jo number caller bhejta hai us par bharosa karna matlab har caller ko bill likhne ki power dena. Is design mein recordPayment(ticketId, paymentId) mein amount parameter hai hi nahi. Amount wahi record hota hai jo beginPayment ya beginExit ne lock karte waqt fix kiya tha: `amountMinor: lock.dueMinor`.

Socho agar signature recordPayment(ticketId, paymentId, amount) hota. Pay station ka ek bug (ya koi bura actor jo station ka code chala raha hai) 1 paisa charge karke 'recordPayment(t, id, 50000)' bol deta, aur lot maan leta ki poora bill pay ho gaya. Ab amount ek hi jagah decide hota hai -- lot ke andar, pricing strategy se, lock ke time par.

Doosra fayda: lock amount ko freeze bhi karta hai. Card reader slow hai aur ek ghanta beet gaya -- money.test.ts ka pehla test clock 1 ghanta aage karta hai aur quote() phir bhi 10000 deta hai. Jo amount gateway ko bheja gaya (quote.dueMinor), wahi record hota hai, toh provider ka charge aur lot ka record match karte hain.

Mutation P23 ('the full fee recorded instead of the locked due amount') 7 tests fail karta hai -- yaani agar dusri payment par poora fee record ho jaaye (sirf due ki jagah), tests pakad lete hain.
why_needed: Money ka amount trust boundary ke andar decide hona chahiye. Caller ka number = caller ki marzi ka bill.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein waiter bill machine se nikalta hai; customer khud bill par amount nahi likhta, chahe woh kitna bhi imaandaar ho.
how_it_works: beginPayment: bill(entry, now) se fee, paid, due nikaalta hai, due 0 ho toh NOTHING_DUE, warna lockEntry() se Lock {kind, at, feeMinor, paidMinor, dueMinor, paymentKey}. recordPayment: lock hona chahiye, dueMinor 0 nahi hona chahiye, paymentId khaali ya repeat nahi; phir Payment {paymentId, amountMinor: lock.dueMinor, at: lock.at}.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: recordPayment() comment: 'The amount is the one fixed by the lock, never a caller's number.' PayStation.pay() aur ExitGate.leave() dono gateway ko quote.dueMinor bhejte hain aur phir sirf recordPayment(ticketId, paymentId) bulaate hain.
advantages: Amount ka ek hi source of truth
Provider ko bheja amount aur record kiya amount same
Slow device ke dauraan price nahi badalta
disadvantages: Partial payment (aadha card, aadha cash) is API se nahi hoti
paymentId abhi bhi caller ka string hai -- uski verification alag problem hai
common_mistakes: API mein amount parameter rakh dena 'flexibility' ke naam par
Record karte waqt dobara price calculate karna (time badal chuka hoga)
Poora fee record karna jab pehle kuch pay ho chuka ho (P23)
follow_up_questions: paymentId bhi fake ho sakta hai -- usko kaise verify karoge?
Partial payment support karna ho toh design kaise badlega?
HTTP API mein yeh rule kaise dikhega?

question: A customer reports a lost ticket. How does the lot stop someone who found or stole that ticket from using it?
answer_hinglish:
reportLost(plate) ek replacement ticket deta hai aur purani id ko maar deta hai. Purana ticket jiske bhi haath mein ho, uska har use TICKET_REPLACED deta hai. 'Lost' ka matlab 'stolen' bhi ho sakta hai -- agar purani id valid rehti, toh chor usi se car le jaata.

Andar kya hota hai: plate normalise karke ticketIdByPlate se entry milti hai. Entry 'reserved' hai toh TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE, 'paying' ya 'exiting' hai toh TICKET_BUSY (beech mein payment ya exit chal raha hai toh replace nahi). Phir naya Ticket banta hai `{ ...old, id: randomUUID(), replaces: old.id }` -- same plate, same spot, same entryAt, toh stay ka bill wahi rehta hai. spot.transfer(old.id, ticket.id) spot ka holder badalta hai (sirf tab jab spot occupied ho aur purane ticket ke paas ho). Purani entry delete, nayi entry mein purani payments carry hoti hain aur penaltyMinor mein lostTicketPenaltyMinor judta hai. Aakhir mein old id `replaced` Set mein jaati hai; parked() us set ko dekh kar TICKET_REPLACED phenkta hai, TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE nahi -- taaki attendant ko pata chale yeh ticket report hua tha.

Jo protect NAHI hota, honestly: (1) ownership check model nahi hai -- README kehta hai attendant documents/plate photo check karta hai, code mein nahi. Koi bhi plate bol kar replacement le sakta hai agar attendant check na kare. (2) Agar chor report se PEHLE nikal gaya, toh replacement kuch nahi bachata. (3) Penalty ek deterrent hai, auth nahi.
why_needed: Bearer ticket mein 'lost' ko handle kiye bina chori ka seedha raasta khula rehta hai.
real_world_analogy: Debit card kho gaya toh bank card block karke naya card deta hai, same account. Purana card ab har jagah decline hota hai, chahe kisi ke bhi paas ho.
how_it_works: Same stay ko naye identifier par move karna + purane identifier ko tombstone karna. Tombstone (replaced Set) ki wajah se error message specific milta hai. Spot transfer guarded hai: SPOT_STATE agar spot kisi aur ke paas hai.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: reportLost(), private `replaced = new Set<string>()`, parked() mein TICKET_REPLACED check. src/spot.ts transfer(). Test money.test.ts 'issues a replacement for the same stay with the penalty, and kills the old ticket' -- penalty 20000, 1 ghante baad bill 25000, beginExit(old.id) aur quote(old.id) dono TICKET_REPLACED. Mutations P8 (old ticket still valid) aur P10 (TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE instead of TICKET_REPLACED) dono 1-1 test se pakde gaye.
advantages: Chura hua ticket turant bekaar
Pehle ki payments nahi khoti (P9 test)
Specific error code se attendant alert ho sakta hai
disadvantages: Ownership verification code mein nahi hai
replaced Set kabhi saaf nahi hota -- lambe process mein badhta rahega
Report se pehle nikal chuka chor nahi rukta
common_mistakes: Lost ticket par naya stay shuru kar dena (entry time reset = sasta bill)
Purana ticket valid chhod dena
Payment ya exit ke beech replace allow karna
follow_up_questions: Ownership check kaise karoge -- ANPR camera plate match?
replaced set ko memory mein bounded kaise rakhoge?
Kya penalty ek fixed amount ho ya daily max?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Replacement + tombstone simple hai aur same stay rakhta hai; cost yeh hai ki identity ka sabse kamzor hissa (attendant ka check) code ke bahar hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Attacker plate bol ke replacement maange: lot dega, kyunki ownership model nahi hai. Chor report se pehle exit kare: koi bachav nahi. reportLost payment ke beech: TICKET_BUSY, kuch nahi badalta (tested).
advanced.alternatives: Plate recognition camera se exit par plate == ticket.plate check; tickets ko customer phone se bind karna; signed tickets jinka revocation list ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare lots / processes: replaced ids ek shared store mein chahiye (DB table ya Redis set with TTL), warna doosra process purani id maan lega.
advanced.production_improvements: Exit par ANPR plate match, reportLost par audit log (kisne, kab, kaunsa document), replaced ids ka TTL (stay khatam hone ke baad hata do).

question: If you plugged in a real payment provider, how would you handle its API credentials?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle seedhi baat: is project mein koi real provider nahi hai aur koi credential exist nahi karta. PaymentGateway ek interface hai, aur uska akela implementation FakePaymentGateway hai jo memory mein charges rakhta hai, koi network call nahi, koi paisa nahi. README ka status line bhi kehta hai 'No real payment provider, no real money, no credentials anywhere.'

Agar real provider lagana ho, toh general practice yeh hai (yahan built nahi): API secret key kabhi code ya git mein nahi. Process ko environment variable ya secret manager (cloud ka secrets service, Vault) se milti hai, startup par ek baar padhi jaati hai, aur missing ho toh process start hi na ho. Test aur live keys alag, aur CI mein sirf test keys. Logs mein key ya card data kabhi print na ho -- error ko log karte waqt request headers strip karo. Key rotate karne ka plan ho. Card number lot ke paas aana hi nahi chahiye: card reader ya provider ka hosted terminal card handle kare, lot ko sirf payment id mile -- isse PCI scope chhota rehta hai.

Design ka fayda yahan dikhta hai: real gateway class sirf charge(request, signal) implement karegi. Credentials us class ke constructor mein inject honge, ParkingLot ko unka pata bhi nahi chalega. Lot sirf paymentId aur amount dekhta hai.
why_needed: Leaked payment key = koi bhi aapke naam se charge/refund kar sakta hai. Yeh sabse costly secret hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ki tijori ki chaabi counter par nahi chipkaate; manager ke paas rehti hai aur har shift ke log ko sirf utna access milta hai jitna chahiye.
how_it_works: Interface boundary: ParkingLot -> PayStation/ExitGate -> PaymentGateway. Secret sirf sabse bahar wali layer (real gateway adapter) tak jaata hai. Domain code testable rehta hai kyunki fake gateway ko koi secret nahi chahiye.
in_this_project: src/payment.ts: interface PaymentGateway { charge(request, signal) }, comment 'No real provider is integrated in this project ... No real money, no real credentials.' src/fake-gateway.ts: FakePaymentGateway 'Moves no money'. Credentials handling poori tarah NOT implemented hai -- upar wala sab generic advice hai.
advantages: Domain code secret-free aur testable
Secret ek jagah inject, rotate karna aasaan
Fake gateway ke saath CI mein koi secret nahi chahiye
disadvantages: Env vars process dump / child process mein leak ho sakte hain -- secret manager behtar
Is repo mein yeh sab sirf advice hai, code nahi
common_mistakes: Key ko config file mein commit kar dena
Error log mein poori HTTP request print kar dena
Live aur test key ek hi env mein
follow_up_questions: Card data lot ke server tak kyun nahi aana chahiye?
Key rotation bina downtime kaise?
Provider ke webhook ko kaise authenticate karoge?

question: Could a caller record a forged or replayed payment id to make a ticket look paid?
answer_hinglish:
Haan, aur yeh is design ki ek honest limit hai. recordPayment(ticketId, paymentId) amount ko caller se nahi leta (woh lock se aata hai), lekin paymentId sirf ek string hai jo caller deta hai. Lot provider se verify nahi karta ki yeh id sach mein ek successful charge hai. Jo bhi code beginPayment ke baad recordPayment(t, 'kuch-bhi') bulaaye, woh ticket ko paid mark kar sakta hai.

Kya check hota hai: id khaali nahi honi chahiye aur ISI ticket par pehle record nahi honi chahiye (INVALID_PAYMENT_ID) -- money.test.ts mein 'p1' dobara record karna refuse hota hai, mutation P15 isko pakadta hai. Lekin same id DOOSRE ticket par record ho sakti hai; global uniqueness check nahi hai. Lock bhi chahiye (PAYMENT_NOT_STARTED), aur due 0 ho toh NOTHING_DUE.

Kyun theek hai is project ke liye: yeh ek in-process library hai, trust boundary process ki boundary hai. PayStation aur ExitGate trusted code hain jo khud chargeWithRetry se aaya id record karte hain. Provider-side replay ke liye idempotency key hai: same key dobara aaye toh fake gateway naya charge nahi karta, pehla result lautata hai; same key different amount ke saath aaye toh refuse.

Production mein (built nahi): recordPayment ko trusted server-side component hi bulaaye, aur payment id ko provider se verify karo (lookup ya signed webhook), amount aur reference (ticket id) match karo, aur payment_id par globally unique constraint lagao.
why_needed: Bill ka 'paid' flag hi exit ki chaabi hai. Agar usko bina proof ke set kiya ja sake toh barrier rule bekaar.
real_world_analogy: Cashier ko koi bhi photocopy wali receipt dikha de aur woh bina bank se check kiye maan le -- yahi risk hai. Asli dukaan receipt number POS system mein verify karti hai.
how_it_works: Payment id ek claim hai, proof nahi. Proof tab banta hai jab issuer (provider) confirm kare: id exist karta hai, status succeeded, amount aur reference match. Replay ka bachav: per-ticket duplicate check (yahan hai) + global unique constraint (yahan nahi) + provider verification (yahan nahi).
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts recordPayment(): `entry.payments.some((p) => p.paymentId === paymentId)` -- sirf is entry ki payments. Reference ticket id gateway ko jaata hai (PaymentRequest.reference) lekin lot wapas check nahi karta. FakePaymentGateway.charge() reused key + different amount/reference par 'idempotency key reused with a different request' phenkta hai (payment.test.ts).
advantages: Same ticket par double record nahi
Amount caller ke haath mein nahi
Provider-side replay idempotency key se safe
disadvantages: Payment id ki authenticity verify nahi hoti
Cross-ticket reuse detect nahi hota
Trust poori tarah in-process callers par
common_mistakes: Payment id ko proof of payment maan lena
Sirf client ke 'success' callback par bill paid mark karna
Idempotency key aur payment id ko ek hi cheez samajhna
follow_up_questions: Provider webhook ka signature kaise verify karte ho?
Global unique payment_id DB mein kaise lagaoge?
Agar verification ke liye provider down ho toh exit rokoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Library ko simple aur synchronous rakhne ke liye recordPayment koi network check nahi karta; iska matlab trust in-process callers par hai. Verification add karna lot ko async bana dega ya ek alag verify step maangega.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Buggy integration galat id record kare: ticket paid dikhega, provider ke paas paisa nahi. Same provider id do tickets par: dono paid, ek hi charge. Dono ko sirf reconciliation (built nahi) pakdega.
advanced.alternatives: recordPayment ke andar provider lookup (async, lock ke andar hi theek hai); ya signed webhook se hi payment record karna; ya lot khud gateway ko call kare taaki id kabhi bahar se na aaye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare stations/processes: payment_id par DB unique index, aur nightly reconciliation job jo provider ki report ko payments table se join kare.
advanced.production_improvements: Payment record ke saath provider ka status/amount/reference store karo, mismatch par alert; payments table par unique(payment_id); audit log ki kaunsa component record kar raha hai.

question: Why is the 'no car leaves unpaid' rule enforced inside the lot instead of inside the exit gate?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki gates bahut saare hain aur unka code badalta rehta hai; lot ek hai. Agar rule gate mein hota, toh har gate -- aur har gate ka har bug -- bina pay kiye bahar jaane ka ek raasta hota. commitExit() khud check karta hai: `if (lock.dueMinor > 0) throw PAYMENT_REQUIRED`. Koi bhi caller, kitna bhi galat likha ho, lot ko 'car gayi' nahi bol sakta jab tak locked due amount record na ho.

ExitGate.leave() bhi apni taraf se check karta hai: card reader (gateway) nahi hai aur due > 0 toh PAYMENT_REQUIRED, barrier device bulaata hi nahi. Lekin yeh convenience hai, guarantee nahi. Mutation P24 ('exit gate without a card reader lets an unpaid car out') mein gate ka check hata diya gaya -- tab bhi 1 test fail hua, kyunki commitExit ne mana kar diya. P1 ('commitExit lets a car out with money due') 2 tests se pakda gaya. PLAN.md ka decision: 'Recommended over the gate checks the payment because then every gate (and every bug in one) would be a way out without paying.'

Security ki bhasha mein yeh defense in depth aur 'enforce invariants at the owner of the state' hai. Receipt ka paidMinor isi wajah se hamesha feeMinor ke barabar hota hai, aur randomized test har receipt par yeh assert karta hai.

Limit: ek physical gate jo lot ko pooche bina barrier khol de, use koi software nahi rok sakta -- device driver trusted hai. Aur recordPayment ka paymentId verify nahi hota (alag sawaal). Rule 'state change' ko rokta hai, hardware ko nahi.
why_needed: Money invariant ek jagah enforce ho toh audit karna, test karna aur trust karna aasaan. Bikhra hua check = bikhra hua bug surface.
real_world_analogy: Toll plaza ke har lane ka operator alag hai, lekin boom barrier central system se signal milne par hi uthta hai -- operator ki galti se gaadi free nahi nikal sakti.
how_it_works: Exit two-phase hai: beginExit (lock + fee fix) -> optional charge + recordPayment (lock.dueMinor = 0) -> barrier device -> commitExit. commitExit lock dekhta hai; due > 0 toh throw, state unchanged (money.test.ts before/after JSON compare). Booth ka exit() bhi yahi path use karta hai: due ho toh cash payment record, phir commitExit.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: commitExit() comment 'The barrier rule lives here, not in the gate: no car leaves while money is due.' src/gates.ts ExitGate.leave(): gateway undefined + due > 0 -> PAYMENT_REQUIRED. Tests: money.test.ts 'commitExit refuses while money is due, and nothing changes' aur 'without a card reader, an unpaid ticket gets PAYMENT_REQUIRED and the barrier stays shut' (opened === 0).
advantages: Ek invariant, ek enforcement point
Naya gate type (ANPR, valet) automatically safe
Mutation testing se proof ki gate ka bug bhi pakda jaata hai (P24)
disadvantages: Physical barrier ko software se bandhna hardware/driver ka kaam hai, yahan nahi
Do jagah check (gate + lot) -- message thoda duplicate
common_mistakes: Sirf UI/gate mein validation rakhna
Gate ke check ko hi security maan lena
commitExit mein dobara price nikaalna (fixed lock ki jagah) -- S19
follow_up_questions: Agar exit gate network ke paar alag service ho toh yeh rule kahan jaayega?
Hardware barrier ko lot ke decision se kaise bind karoge?
Emergency mein (fire) barriers khulne hain -- rule ko kaise bypass karoge, audit ke saath?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Rule lot mein = gate dumb aur replaceable; cost yeh ki lot ko payment ka concept samajhna padta hai (lock, due). Gate mein rule = lot simple, lekin har gate trusted.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Gate ka check galat: commitExit bachaata hai (P24). Lot ka check galat: P1, sab gates se free exit. Device driver lot ko pooche bina khol de: software se nahi rukta.
advanced.alternatives: Separate 'payment service' jo exit token sign kare aur gate sirf signed token par khule; ya DB constraint/trigger jo unpaid ticket ko closed mark na hone de.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-process: rule DB transaction mein -- UPDATE tickets SET status='exited' WHERE id=? AND due=0 -- taaki koi process skip na kar sake.
advanced.production_improvements: Emergency override ek explicit, audited API ho; barrier controller sirf lot se mila one-time open command maane; har PAYMENT_REQUIRED ko metric banao (gate bug ka signal).

question: Why does each lock get a fresh random idempotency key, and why must every retry reuse it?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag rules hain aur dono security/money ke liye zaroori hain. Pehla: ek lock ke andar har retry SAME key bheje -- warna lost response ke baad retry naya charge ban jaata hai (double charge). Doosra: har naya lock NAYI key le -- warna ek purani payment ka result agli payment par chipak jaata hai.

lockEntry() har beginPayment/beginExit par `paymentKey: randomUUID()` banata hai aur woh quote mein bahar aata hai. PayStation aur ExitGate us key ko PaymentRequest.idempotencyKey mein daal kar chargeWithRetry ko dete hain, jo loop mein wahi request object baar baar bhejta hai.

Mutations dikhate hain kyun: P2 ('retries use a new idempotency key') 7 tests fail karta hai -- lose-response ke baad second charge. P22 ('the same payment key for every lock of a ticket') 3 tests fail -- socho customer ne 50 pay kiye, window ke baad 50 aur due hua; same key se provider kehta 'yeh toh pehle ho chuka' aur pehla id lauta deta (ya amount alag hone par refuse karta), aur lot ek hi id dobara record karne ki koshish karta.

Key random kyun, ticket id + counter kyun nahi? Predictable key se koi doosra caller (same provider account par) kisi aur ki key guess karke uska result 'claim' kar sakta hai ya collide kar sakta hai. Random UUID per lock collision-free aur unguessable hai.

Fake gateway mein ek extra guard: same key + different amount ya reference = error, jaise real providers karte hain.
why_needed: Idempotency key hi woh cheez hai jo 'retry' ko safe banati hai. Galat scope (bahut chhota ya bahut bada) dono double charge ya wrong record dete hain.
real_world_analogy: Courier ka AWB number: ek parcel ka ek number, chahe tracking kitni baar bhi karo. Naya parcel bhejoge toh naya number -- purana number reuse karoge toh system purane parcel ka status dikhayega.
how_it_works: Key ka scope = ek 'intended payment' = ek lock. Lock ke andar amount fixed hai (lock.dueMinor), isliye same key + same amount + same reference har retry par. Lock khatam (record ya abort) -> key bhi khatam; agli payment naya lock, nayi key.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts lockEntry(): `paymentKey: randomUUID()`. src/pay-station.ts aur src/gates.ts: `{ idempotencyKey: quote.paymentKey, amountMinor: quote.dueMinor, reference: quote.ticket.id }`. src/fake-gateway.ts charge(): byKey lookup, mismatch par 'idempotency key reused with a different request'. Test payment.test.ts 'lost response, then a retry with the same key: one charge, the caller gets its id' (calls 2, charges 1).
advantages: Lost response ke baad retry safe
Har payment intent alag pehchaan
Unguessable key
disadvantages: Key sirf lock ke dauraan yaad hai; abort ke baad key kho jaati hai (PAYMENT_UNKNOWN ka issue)
Provider ko key store karni padti hai (unka cost)
common_mistakes: Har retry par nayi key (P2)
Ticket id ko hi key bana dena (P22 jaisa bug)
Key ko payment id samajh lena
follow_up_questions: PAYMENT_UNKNOWN ke baad customer dobara pay kare toh kaunsi key jaayegi?
Provider key kitni der yaad rakhta hai aur iska design par kya asar?
Key ko DB mein kab persist karoge -- charge se pehle ya baad?

question: This lot keeps everything in memory. If you had to persist it, what tables would you create?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle clear kar doon: is project mein DB nahi hai. Sab kuch ek Node process ki memory mein hai -- README ki 'NOT implemented' list mein 'Persistence and more than one process' likha hai. Process restart = saari parked cars ka record gaya. Toh yeh 'kaise karta' wala answer hai.

Main teen core tables banata, jo seedhe in-memory structures ko replace karti hain:

1. spots (id, level, position, size, state, held_by_ticket) -- ParkingLot ka `spots` array aur ParkingSpot ka state/holder. state ek CHECK constraint: free / reserved / occupied.
2. tickets (id UUID primary key, plate, vehicle, spot_id, entry_at, status, replaces, penalty_minor, lock_kind, lock_at, lock_fee_minor, lock_due_minor, payment_key) -- `entries` Map ki Entry aur uska Lock. status: reserved / active / paying / exiting / exited / replaced. Exit ke baad row delete nahi karta (memory wala code delete karta hai), status 'exited' karta -- history aur disputes ke liye chahiye.
3. payments (payment_id, ticket_id, amount_minor BIGINT, at, idempotency_key, method card/cash) -- Entry.payments array.

Availability board ke liye `rows` Map ko table banane ki zaroorat nahi -- spots par GROUP BY level, size, state se nikal sakta hai, ya ek counter table jo same transaction mein update ho.

Money hamesha integer minor units mein (BIGINT), kabhi FLOAT/DOUBLE nahi -- code bhi yahi karta hai.
why_needed: Real lot mein process restart, deploy, crash hote rehte hain. Memory-only data matlab har restart par 'andar kaun hai' bhool jaana.
real_world_analogy: Abhi lot ka register ek attendant ke dimaag mein hai. Shift badli toh sab bhool gaye. Tables = ek likha hua register jo shift ke baad bhi rehta hai.

question: How would you enforce 'one active ticket per plate' in a database?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai; yeh rule abhi `ticketIdByPlate` Map se enforce hota hai. reserve() pehle plate normalise karta hai, phir `if (this.ticketIdByPlate.has(plate)) throw ALREADY_PARKED`. Synchronous method hai, toh check aur set ke beech koi aur code nahi chal sakta.

DB mein yeh check-then-insert race ban jaata hai: do gate processes dono SELECT karke 'plate nahi hai' dekh sakte hain aur dono INSERT kar dete hain. Isliye check ko constraint mein badalna chahiye: ek partial unique index -- UNIQUE (plate) WHERE status IN ('reserved','active','paying','exiting'). Exited ya replaced tickets is index mein nahi aate, toh same car kal phir aa sakti hai, aur replacement ticket bhi (purana 'replaced' ho chuka hoga same transaction mein).

Ab INSERT khud race jeet ya haar jaata hai: doosra INSERT unique violation deta hai, jise app ALREADY_PARKED mein map karti hai. Koi SELECT pehle karne ki zaroorat nahi.

Do details jo code se aati hain: (1) plate ko DB mein normalised form mein hi store karo -- normalizePlate() 'mh 12-ab 1234' ko 'MH12AB1234' banata hai. Agar raw store kiya toh unique index do alag strings dekhega aur ek car do tickets le legi (stage 1 mutation 'plate not normalised'). (2) 'reserved' status bhi index mein ho, kyunki code mein bhi same plate doosre gate par entering ho toh ALREADY_PARKED hai.

Postgres mein partial index milta hai; MySQL mein ek generated column (active_plate = plate jab active, warna NULL) par unique index se same effect.
why_needed: Ek plate do tickets = ek car do spots block kare, ya ek ticket se exit karke doosra baad mein misuse ho.
real_world_analogy: Hotel mein ek guest ID par ek waqt mein ek hi room check-in. Reception register mein yeh rule likha hai, sirf receptionist ki yaad par nahi chhoda.
how_it_works: Partial unique index sirf matching rows ko index karta hai. INSERT/UPDATE par DB atomically uniqueness check karta hai -- yeh check-then-act ko ek atomic step bana deta hai, jo yahan JavaScript ka synchronous block karta hai.

question: How would the spot claim (reserve) work across several gate processes sharing one database?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai aur ek hi Node process hai. Wahan claim safe hai kyunki reserve() synchronous hai: free spot dhoondhna, spot.reserve(ticket.id), entries/plate map update -- sab ek block mein, beech mein koi await nahi. README khud kehta hai: kai processes DB share karein toh claim DB mein chahiye -- 'a conditional UPDATE or a unique constraint on the spot' -- same idea, state jahan rehti hai wahan. Yeh built nahi hai.

Main conditional UPDATE use karta: `UPDATE spots SET state='reserved', held_by=$ticket WHERE id=$spot AND state='free'`. Affected rows 1 = claim jeeta, 0 = kisi aur gate ne pehle le liya; tab agla candidate try karo. Yeh ek compare-and-set hai jo DB atomically karta hai -- wahi jo in-memory ParkingSpot.reserve() ka guard `if (this.current !== 'free') throw SPOT_STATE` karta hai.

Candidate kaise chunoge? FreeSpotIndex ka min-heap memory mein hai; DB mein ek index (size, state, level, position) par `SELECT ... WHERE size=$s AND state='free' ORDER BY level, position LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` -- SKIP LOCKED se do gates same row par wait nahi karte, alag-alag free spot uthate hain. Spot claim + ticket insert (status reserved) + plate uniqueness ek hi transaction mein, taaki 'check everything, then change' wala guarantee DB mein bhi rahe: kuch fail ho toh sab rollback.

Phir device ka slow kaam transaction ke BAHAR, jaise code mein: claim commit, device await, phir confirm (reserved -> occupied) ya cancel (-> free). Transaction ko printer ke dauraan open mat rakho -- yahi 'mutex ke bajaye claim' wala decision hai.
why_needed: Do processes ka in-memory check ek doosre ko nahi dikhta. Bina DB-level claim ke last spot do cars ko mil jaayega -- wahi bug jo gates.test.ts naive gates se dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Do receptionist ek hi room ko do guests ko de sakte hain agar dono apni copy dekh rahe hain. Central board par 'room 101: taken' sticker wahi lagata hai jo pehle pahunche -- baaki ko sticker laga hua milta hai.
how_it_works: Optimistic claim: WHERE state='free' guard ke saath UPDATE; rowcount se pata chalta hai jeete ya nahi. Alternative: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED se candidate lock karo, phir update. Dono mein atomic unit DB ka row-level lock hai, JS event loop nahi.

In sab ko DB ka conditional UPDATE + index replace karega.

question: How would you design the payments table, including the idempotency key?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai; payments abhi har Entry ka `payments: Payment[]` array hain, aur Payment mein sirf paymentId, amountMinor aur at hai. Idempotency key (paymentKey) sirf lock ke andar rehti hai, record nahi hoti. Persist karte waqt main yeh design karta:

payments (payment_id TEXT, ticket_id UUID, idempotency_key UUID, amount_minor BIGINT CHECK > 0, method card/cash, at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at).

Constraints: (1) payment_id UNIQUE -- code abhi sirf ek ticket ke andar duplicate rokta hai (INVALID_PAYMENT_ID), DB poore system mein rokega. (2) idempotency_key UNIQUE -- ek lock = ek payment, toh ek key par do rows kabhi nahi. Agar app ka retry ya do processes same payment do baar record karne aayein, doosra insert fail hoga. (3) amount BIGINT minor units, kabhi float nahi -- pricing.ts ka comment: 3 x 0.10 kabhi 0.30000000000000004 nahi banna chahiye.

Ek important badlaav: idempotency key ko charge se PEHLE persist karna chahiye -- ek 'payment_attempts' row (key, ticket, amount, status pending) jo provider call se pehle commit ho. Kyun? Code mein PAYMENT_UNKNOWN par lock release ho jaata hai aur key kho jaati hai; README kehta hai paisa shayad kat chuka ho aur reconciliation built nahi. Key DB mein ho toh baad mein provider se poocha ja sakta hai 'is key ka kya hua'.

`at` column code jaisa hi -- lock ka time, payment ka nahi -- kyunki exit window wahin se ginta hai.
why_needed: Payments table money ka ledger hai. Duplicate ya missing row = customer ka double charge ya free exit.
real_world_analogy: Bank passbook: har entry ka unique transaction number, amount paise mein, aur ek baar likhi entry dobara nahi likhi jaati.
how_it_works: Unique constraints idempotency ko storage layer mein le aate hain: app retry kare toh DB duplicate ko reject karta hai. Pending attempt row 'intent' record karta hai taaki unknown outcome ko baad mein resolve kiya ja sake.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: interface Payment { paymentId, amountMinor, at }, recordPayment() mein per-entry duplicate check, lockEntry() mein paymentKey. Booth exit() cash payment ko `cash-${randomUUID()}` id deta hai -- DB mein method column se yeh string prefix ki zaroorat nahi rahegi.

CREATE TABLE payment_attempts (
  idempotency_key UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  ticket_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(id),
  amount_minor BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_minor > 0),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','succeeded','declined','unknown')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE payments (
  payment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  idempotency_key UUID UNIQUE REFERENCES payment_attempts(idempotency_key),
  ticket_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(id),
  amount_minor BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_minor > 0),
  method TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('card','cash')),
  at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

Unknown outcome ke liye key saved
Ledger auditable

question: How would you persist the payment and exit locks so that a crashed process does not leave a ticket locked forever?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai, aur in-memory version mein yeh problem pehle se hai: agar PayStation ya ExitGate beginPayment/beginExit ke baad mar jaaye, ticket 'paying'/'exiting' mein atak jaata hai aur har agla try TICKET_BUSY. README ki NOT implemented list kehti hai koi expiry sweep nahi hai; timeouts hung device/provider cover karte hain, crashed gate nahi. Memory-only hone ki wajah se abhi process crash = sab state gayi, toh yeh problem chhupi hui hai; DB aate hi saamne aayegi.

Persist karte waqt lock ko lease banata: tickets par lock_kind, lock_at, lock_due_minor, payment_key, aur lock_expires_at. beginPayment = `UPDATE tickets SET status='paying', lock_... , lock_expires_at = now() + interval WHERE id=$1 AND status='active'` -- rowcount 0 = TICKET_BUSY ya not active. Yeh wahi check hai jo unlocked() karta hai, ab atomic DB par.

Expiry ka rule soch samajh kar: 'paying' lock expire karna tabhi safe hai jab us lock ka payment_attempt resolve ho chuka ho. Agar provider call pending/unknown hai aur hum lock chhod dein, customer naye lock aur nayi key se dobara pay karega -- double charge (wahi PAYMENT_UNKNOWN wala gap). Toh sweep pehle provider se key ka status poochhe (reconciliation), phir: charged mila toh payment record karo, nahi mila toh abort.

'exiting' lock ka expiry: payment record ho chuki ho toh woh rehti hai (code mein bhi abortExit payments nahi hatata, P11), sirf lock hatta hai. Barrier khula ya nahi -- woh hardware se poochhna padega.

lock_expires_at device timeout + retries se lamba hona chahiye: defaults se ek exit 3 x 10 s charge + 10 s barrier tak le sakta hai.
why_needed: Bina lease ke ek crash permanent damage hai: car andar, ticket locked, koi exit nahi -- attendant ko manually DB edit karna padega.
real_world_analogy: Library ki kitaab issue ki aur borrower gaayab -- due date (lease) hoti hai, warna kitaab hamesha 'issued' dikhegi. Lekin due date nikalne par bhi pehle check karte ho ki kahin woh lauta toh nahi chuka.
how_it_works: Lease = lock + expiry. Owner kaam khatam karke clear karta hai; owner mar jaaye toh expiry ke baad koi aur sweep kar sakta hai. Fencing: commit karte waqt WHERE payment_key=$key, taaki expire hua purana owner baad mein aakar galat lock par record na kare.

Lock expiry NOT implemented.

   SET status = 'paying', lock_at = now(), lock_due_minor = $due,
       payment_key = $key, lock_expires_at = now() + interval '2 minutes'
 WHERE id = $ticket AND status = 'active';         -- 0 rows -> TICKET_BUSY / not active

-- record only if we still own the lock (fencing by key)
UPDATE tickets SET status = 'active', payment_key = NULL, lock_expires_at = NULL
 WHERE id = $ticket AND payment_key = $key;

Fencing se stale owner safe
Same lock semantics, ab multi-process

Expiry galat chuni toh slow-but-alive gate ka lock chhin jaayega
common_mistakes: Expiry par bina provider check kiye lock chhod dena
Lease ko device timeout se chhota rakhna
Fencing ke bina record karna

question: Recording a payment and telling other systems about it are two writes. How would you avoid losing one of them (outbox pattern)?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai aur koi external system bhi nahi; events sirf in-process EventQueue se display boards tak jaate hain, aur woh lot ki state change ke BAAD emit hote hain (changeFree() 'last'). Ek hi process aur ek hi memory hai, toh 'state change hua par event nahi gaya' wala gap abhi nahi dikhta.

DB + doosre systems (accounting, receipts email, analytics, board service) aate hi dual-write problem aati hai: payments table mein row likhi aur phir message broker ko publish kiya -- beech mein crash hua toh DB mein payment hai par accounting ko pata nahi. Ulta order kiya toh event gaya par payment rollback.

Outbox pattern: same DB transaction mein payments row AUR ek outbox row (event type 'PaymentRecorded', payload) likho. Commit atomic hai, toh dono ya koi nahi. Ek alag relay process outbox poll karta hai (ya CDC se padhta hai), broker ko publish karta hai, aur sent mark karta hai. Delivery at-least-once hoti hai, isliye consumers event id par idempotent hone chahiye -- wahi soch jo yahan provider ke saath idempotency key mein hai.

Provider call ke saath outbox kaam nahi karta (provider hamare DB transaction mein nahi aata). Uske liye order: attempt row (key, pending) commit -> provider call -> result row + outbox ek transaction mein. Crash beech mein ho toh pending row reconciliation job ko batati hai kya check karna hai.

Lot ke andar ka ordering rule (pehle state complete, phir event) outbox mein bhi rehta hai: event tabhi bahar jaata hai jab commit ho chuka.
why_needed: Money events kho jaayein toh books mismatch: provider ne charge kiya, lot ne record kiya, lekin accounting mein nahi. Ya ulta: accounting mein hai, lot mein nahi.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan mein bill banate hi usi register page par 'courier ko bhejna hai' ka note likh do. Peon din mein register dekh ke parcel bhejta hai. Bill aur note ek saath likhe gaye, toh kuch chhootta nahi -- peon do baar bhej de toh customer duplicate ignore kare.
how_it_works: Transactional outbox: business write + event write ek transaction. Relay: SELECT unsent FROM outbox ORDER BY id -> publish -> UPDATE sent. Consumers dedupe by event id. Ordering per ticket chahiye toh partition key = ticket id.

Broker down ho toh bhi payment record ho jaati hai, event baad mein
Same ordering rule jo in-process EventQueue mein hai
disadvantages: Relay ek aur moving part

Event latency badhti hai (polling)

question: How would you make the lost-ticket replacement atomic in a database?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein DB nahi hai. In-memory reportLost() kai cheezein ek synchronous block mein karta hai: naya ticket, spot.transfer(old, new), purani entry delete, nayi entry with purani payments aur penalty, ticketIdByPlate update, aur old id `replaced` Set mein. Kyunki beech mein koi await nahi, koi doosra caller aadhi-adhuri state nahi dekh sakta. Aur saare checks (plate known, status active, spot held by old ticket) pehle hote hain.

DB mein yeh ek transaction banega, aur har check ek conditional statement:

1. `UPDATE tickets SET status='replaced' WHERE id=$old AND status='active' RETURNING spot_id, entry_at, penalty_minor` -- 0 rows = TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE ya TICKET_BUSY (paying/exiting mein replace nahi, jaise code mein).
2. INSERT naya ticket: same plate, spot, entry_at; replaces=$old; penalty = purana + lostTicketPenalty; status active. Partial unique index on active plate theek rehta hai kyunki purana ab 'replaced' hai.
3. `UPDATE spots SET held_by=$new WHERE id=$spot AND held_by=$old AND state='occupied'` -- yeh spot.transfer() ka guard hai.
4. Payments: memory mein array nayi entry par move hota hai. DB mein payments ko stay se jodna behtar hai -- ek stay_id column, ya replacement chain follow karna. Main stay_id rakhta: dono tickets same stay ke, payments stay par, bill stay par.

'replaced' Set ki jagah status='replaced' row khud hai -- TICKET_REPLACED dena aasaan, aur memory mein badhte Set ka problem khatam. Commit ke baad hi naya ticket print ho.
why_needed: Aadha replacement sabse kharab state hai: naya ticket bana par purana bhi active, ya spot kisi ke paas nahi. Chor ya bug dono ka fayda.
real_world_analogy: SIM swap: naya SIM activate aur purana deactivate ek hi operation mein hota hai. Agar beech mein ruk jaaye aur dono chalein, toh fraud ka raasta.
how_it_works: Transaction + conditional updates = 'check everything, then change' ka DB version. Row counts guards ka kaam karte hain; koi bhi 0 aaye toh ROLLBACK, kuch nahi badla -- code ka 'a failed call changes nothing' rule.

Test money.test.ts 'keeps payments made before the loss' (paid 5000, fee 25000, due 20000) aur refusals wala test state before/after compare karta hai.

question: The card provider goes down for 20 minutes during evening rush. What happens at the exits, and what would you do?
answer_hinglish:
Code ke hisaab se: har exit gate par beginExit ticket lock karta hai, chargeWithRetry 3 attempts karta hai (har ek 10 s timeout, beech mein 200 ms), sab fail -> PAYMENT_UNKNOWN. ExitGate.leave() catch mein abortExit karta hai: ticket wapas active, kuch record nahi, barrier band, car andar. Pay station par same: abortPayment, PAYMENT_UNKNOWN. Har car ke liye yeh sabse bura case mein ~30 s ka intezaar hai (defaults se calculate kiya, measure nahi kiya).

Provider ka error 'down' wala hai (fail) ya timeout -- dono 'unknown' maane jaate hain kyunki code decline ke alawa sab ko unknown treat karta hai. Yeh sahi hai: outage mein kuch charges shayad ho bhi gaye hon.

Raasta jo code mein HAI: attendant booth. lot.exit(ticketId) synchronous hai, due amount ko `cash-...` payment ke roop mein record karta hai aur car chhod deta hai. Toh outage mein cash lane chalu kar sakte ho; receipt mein dikhega ki cash se pay hua.

Jo NAHI hai (production mein add karna): circuit breaker -- 3 x 10 s har car par barbaad karne ke bajaye, lagatar failures ke baad gateway turant 'unavailable' bole aur gate screen 'cash lane use karein' dikhaye. Provider status ka metric/alert. Aur PAYMENT_UNKNOWN cases ki list, kyunki un cars se dobara charge karne se pehle reconciliation chahiye -- warna double charge (yeh built nahi). Kuch lots outage mein 'barrier khol do, baad mein bill bhejo' policy rakhte hain -- woh business decision hai, aur yahan commitExit PAYMENT_REQUIRED ki wajah se allow hi nahi karega bina explicit override ke.
why_needed: Payment provider external dependency hai; uska down hona exit ko rokta hai. Rush mein yeh queue aur gussa dono banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Petrol pump par card machine band -- staff 'cash only' board lagata hai. Har customer ka card 3 baar try karke 1 minute barbaad nahi karta.
how_it_works: Retry loop: attempt -> withTimeout(10 s) -> error -> sleep(200 ms) -> next. Last error ParkingError PAYMENT_UNKNOWN ke cause mein. Gate: catch -> abortExit -> rethrow ParkingError. Booth: beginExit -> recordPayment('cash-uuid') -> commitExit, sab synchronous.

Tests: payment.test.ts 'transient failures are retried; all attempts failing is PAYMENT_UNKNOWN with the last cause'; money.test.ts booth test (paymentId /^cash-/). Circuit breaker NOT implemented.

question: An exit gate process crashes right after charging a card but before recordPayment. What state is the system in?
answer_hinglish:
Do levels par jawab hai. Is project mein sab ek Node process ki memory mein hai -- process crash matlab poora ParkingLot gaya, saare tickets, spots, payments. Restart par lot khaali hai. Toh in-memory design mein 'crash' ka jawab hai: sab kuch kho gaya; isliye persistence production ki pehli zaroorat hai (built nahi).

Ab maan lo state persist thi (jaise DB wale sawaalon mein), aur sirf gate ka process mara. Timeline: beginExit ne ticket 'exiting' lock kiya aur paymentKey banayi; chargeWithRetry ne provider se charge karwaya; answer aane ke baad, recordPayment se pehle crash. Ab: provider ke paas paisa hai, lot ke paas nahi. Ticket 'exiting' mein atka hai -- har naya beginExit TICKET_BUSY. Koi expiry sweep nahi hai (README NOT implemented list), toh yeh hamesha atka rahega. Timeout (withTimeout) sirf hung device/provider ko cover karta hai, mare hue caller ko nahi.

Recovery ke liye chahiye: (1) lock ki lease/expiry; (2) lock ki paymentKey persist ho; (3) sweep provider se poochhe 'is key se charge hua?' -- haan toh recordPayment us payment id ke saath, nahi toh abort; (4) tab ticket active, aur customer bina dobara charge ke nikal sake. Idempotency key yahan bhi kaam aati hai: sweep agar same key se charge 'retry' kare, provider pehla payment lautayega, naya charge nahi.

Jo code achha karta hai: agar crash ki jagah barrier fail hota (process zinda), toh abortExit payment ko recorded chhodta hai aur agla try kuch nahi charge karta -- tested.
why_needed: Crash ke beech wali state hi woh jagah hai jahan paise kho jaate hain ya double charge hote hain. Interviewer yahi dekhna chahta hai ki aap 'happy path' ke bahar soch sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: ATM ne paisa account se kaat liya, notes nikalne se pehle machine band. Bank ka reconciliation baad mein dekhta hai ki notes nikle ya nahi, aur reverse karta hai. Bina us process ke customer ka paisa gaya.
how_it_works: Do-phase exit: lock -> external side effect (charge) -> local record -> device -> commit. Side effect aur local record ke beech crash = 'in-doubt' state. Resolve karne ke liye durable intent (key) + external system se query + timeout-based takeover chahiye.
in_this_project: src/gates.ts ExitGate.leave(): beginExit -> chargeWithRetry -> recordPayment -> device.open -> commitExit. src/parking-lot.ts Lock.paymentKey, abortExit() comment 'Payments recorded during the exit stay recorded'. money.test.ts 'paid at the gate, then the barrier failed: the next try does not charge again' (gateway.calls 1). Crash recovery, persistence, lock expiry: NOT implemented.

Barrier failure (non-crash) already sahi handle hota hai
Lock ki wajah se doosra gate beech mein ghus nahi sakta
disadvantages: In-memory: crash = sab kuch gaya

Reconciliation nahi

Recovery mein nayi key se dobara charge
Lock ko bina provider check ke chhod dena

question: With real card readers at the exit, how long can a driver wait in the worst case, and how would you tune it?
answer_hinglish:
Code ke defaults se calculate karo (yeh measured number nahi hai, sirf arithmetic hai): chargeWithRetry -- attempts 3, har attempt ka timeout 10_000 ms, attempts ke beech retryDelayMs 200. Worst case: 3 x 10 s + 2 x 0.2 s = 30.4 s sirf payment mein. Phir barrier device ka withTimeout, default 10 s. Toh ek bahut bure din mein ek car ~40 s tak gate par khadi reh sakti hai, aur peeche queue.

Tuning ke knobs code mein hain: ExitGateOptions mein `timeoutMs` (device) aur `payment: RetryOptions` (attempts, timeoutMs, retryDelayMs) -- dono constructor se aate hain, toh har gate alag tune ho sakta hai. Tests mein retryDelayMs 0 use hota hai speed ke liye.

Kaise chunoge: per-attempt timeout provider ke real latency distribution se -- typically p99 ke thoda upar, warna slow-but-successful charges ko timeout karke unnecessarily 'unknown' bana doge. Note: timeout ke baad bhi charge shayad ho gaya ho; retry same key se hai toh safe hai, lekin har timeout ek extra call hai. Attempts kam (2) aur exit par 'pay station ya booth use karein' message -- driver ka time zyada qeemti hai. Retry delay mein jitter/exponential backoff nahi hai abhi -- fixed 200 ms; outage mein sab gates ek saath retry karenge.

Ek jaruri baat: device ko AbortSignal maanna padega. withTimeout timeout par controller.abort() karta hai; agar real barrier driver signal ignore karke baad mein khul gaya, toh lot ke hisaab se exit abort hua par car nikal gayi. README kehta hai fakes signal maante hain, real hardware is project mein nahi.
why_needed: Exit par har second queue banata hai. Timeouts aur retries ka budget user experience aur double-charge risk dono decide karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Toll plaza par FASTag na chale toh operator 3 baar scan karta hai, phir cash lane bhejta hai. 10 baar scan karega toh peeche 50 gaadiyan.
how_it_works: withTimeout: AbortController + setTimeout + Promise.race; finally mein clearTimeout. sleep(ms) retry delay. Timeout = reject + abort signal; late answer ignore hota hai.
in_this_project: src/payment.ts RetryOptions aur chargeWithRetry defaults; src/gates.ts DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000, ExitGateOptions { gateway, payment }; src/timeout.ts withTimeout, sleep. Tests payment.test.ts 'a hanging gateway is timed out and aborted, then retried' (fake timers, timeoutMs 1000) aur 'waits retryDelayMs between attempts' (199 ms par calls 1, 200 par 2).

Timeout abort signal bhejta hai
Retry same key se -- safe
disadvantages: Fixed delay, no backoff/jitter
Worst case ~40 s (computed) gate par
Driver ko progress feedback ka koi hook nahi
common_mistakes: Timeout provider latency se chhota rakhna
Retries badha kar 'reliability' badhana
AbortSignal ignore karne wala device driver

question: A customer was overcharged and asks for a refund. How does this system handle it?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: refunds is project mein implement nahi hain. README ki NOT implemented list mein 'A real payment provider, refunds, and reconciliation' likha hai. PaymentGateway interface mein sirf charge() hai, koi refund() nahi, aur lot ka koi method payment ko reverse nahi karta. Payment record frozen object hai aur ticket nikalte hi entry memory se delete ho jaati hai -- toh exit ke baad us ticket ki payments lot se poochhi bhi nahi ja sakti (paymentsFor TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE deta hai). Sirf customer ke paas Receipt bachti hai jisme payments list hai.

Kaise banata: (1) Pehle durable record -- exited tickets aur payments ko persist karna, warna refund kis cheez ka? (2) PaymentGateway mein refund(request, signal) jisme apni idempotency key ho (refund ke liye nayi key, original payment id reference ke saath) -- wahi lost-response problem refunds par bhi hai, double refund bhi utna hi bura. (3) Refund ek naya ledger entry hai, original payment ko edit/delete nahi karna: refunds table (refund_id, payment_id, amount_minor, reason, approved_by). Sum of refunds <= payment amount ka check. (4) Authorization: refund attendant/manager ka action hai, audit log ke saath, kyunki yeh paisa bahar bhejne ka raasta hai.

Overcharge kaise hua hoga, yeh bhi dekhna: code mein pricing monotonic hai aur amount lock se aata hai, toh common cause hoga PAYMENT_UNKNOWN ke baad customer ka dobara pay karna (pehla charge ho chuka tha). Wahan refund se pehle reconciliation chahiye.
why_needed: Refund customer trust aur legal requirement dono hai. Bina refund path ke har galti manual bank process ban jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan mein return counter alag hota hai, manager ki sign ke saath. Cashier bill ko mita nahi deta, naya 'credit note' banata hai.
how_it_works: Refund = reverse money flow, apni idempotency, apna ledger entry, apna authorization. Original payment immutable; net paid = payments - refunds.

question: What would you monitor and alert on if this lot ran in production with real gates and a real provider?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest: is project mein koi metrics, logging pipeline ya alerting nahi hai. Errors ParkingError ke code ke saath throw hote hain aur listener errors console.error par jaate hain -- bas. Lekin code ke error codes hi achhe metrics ban jaate hain, kyunki har failure ka ek machine-readable code hai.

Main yeh dekhta:

Money (sabse important): PAYMENT_UNKNOWN count/rate -- har ek ek possible 'paisa kata, record nahi'. Ek nightly reconciliation: provider ki report ka total == lot ke recorded payments ka total. Yeh wahi invariant hai jo invariants.test.ts har seed ke end mein check karta hai (fake.totalChargedMinor() == recorded sum) -- production mein yeh test nahi, job hai. Decline rate (achanak badhe toh card reader ya provider issue). PAYMENT_REQUIRED at commitExit -- normal flow mein gate khud pehle rok deta hai, toh commitExit tak pahunchna gate bug ka signal hai.

Gates: DEVICE_FAILED rate per gate (printer jam, barrier stuck), device/provider latency p50/p99, timeouts. TICKET_BUSY spikes -- copied tickets ya stuck locks. Lock age: 'paying'/'exiting' mein kitni der se -- crash ke baad atke locks (expiry nahi hai, toh yeh alert zaroori).

Capacity: LOT_FULL rate, reserved spots ki age (gate crash ke baad atki reservation, sweep nahi hai), board vs actual drift (tests mein board = availability(); production mein periodic compare).

Security: TICKET_REPLACED attempts (chura hua ticket use ho raha hai), reportLost frequency per attendant.

Har alert actionable ho: UNKNOWN > 0 -> reconciliation queue; lock age > N min -> attendant ko page.
why_needed: Money systems silently galat hote hain -- koi crash nahi, bas totals match nahi. Monitoring hi bataati hai.
real_world_analogy: Petrol pump ka manager shift end par meter reading aur cash/card total milata hai. Farak aaya toh usi din pakda, mahine baad nahi.
how_it_works: Error codes -> counters (labels: code, gate). Latency -> histograms. Invariants -> periodic jobs (reconciliation). State ages -> gauges from DB queries. Alerts on rates and on any money mismatch.

Metrics/alerting NOT implemented.

Money invariant ka test ready-made reconciliation spec hai
Per-gate labels se hardware issue isolate

Reconciliation ke liye provider report chahiye -- fake mein nahi

PAYMENT_UNKNOWN ko normal failure ki tarah ignore karna
Har error par page -- alert fatigue

question: A driver pays at the pay station, then takes 25 minutes to get to the exit. What does the exit charge?
answer_hinglish:
Sirf extra time ka paisa, pehle wala hissa dobara kabhi nahi. Exit window default 15 minute hai (exitWindowMinutes). Payment ke 15 minute ke andar exit kiya toh stay payment ke time tak priced hai -- kuch due nahi. Window ke baad bill = fee(ab tak ka poora stay) - pehle se paid.

Example test se (car 5000 per started hour, window 15): car 90 minute baad pay karti hai = 2 started hours = 10000 paid. 105 min + 1 ms par (window se 1 ms bahar) bhi 2 started hours hi hain, toh due 0. 125 minute par 3 started hours = 15000 fee, 10000 paid, 5000 due. Toh 25 minute baad (115 min total) agar teesra ghanta abhi shuru nahi hua, toh 0; shuru ho gaya toh ek ghante ka 5000.

Yeh ExitGate mein card reader ho toh wahi charge ho jaata hai; card reader na ho toh PAYMENT_REQUIRED aur driver ko wapas pay station ya booth jaana padega.

Code mein yeh bill() karta hai: aakhri payment ka `at` dekhta hai; agar now <= lastPaidAt + window toh price us payment ke time par nikalta hai, warna abhi ke time par; phir paid ghata deta hai aur Math.max(0, ...) se negative nahi hone deta. Window ka boundary inclusive hai -- 'exactly at the end of the window' test 0 deta hai, aur mutation P4 (boundary exclusive) 1 test se pakda gaya. Doosri payment apni khud ki window kholti hai (tested).
why_needed: Pay-then-exit lot ka normal flow hai. Agar window na ho toh har customer ko pay karte hi sprint karna padega; agar difference na ho toh customer double pay karega.
real_world_analogy: Mall parking ka 'paid ticket, 15 min mein exit karo' wala rule. Der hui toh sirf extra ghante ka, poora dobara nahi.
how_it_works: priceAt = (last payment exists && now <= lastPaidAt + window) ? max(lastPaidAt, entryAt) : now. fee = pricing.fee(entry, priceAt) + penalty. due = max(0, fee - paid).
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts private bill(): `const priceAt = lastPaidAt !== undefined && now <= lastPaidAt + this.exitWindowMs ? ... : now`. Option exitWindowMinutes default 15 (nonNegativeInt, INVALID_OPTION). Tests money.test.ts 'paid at the station: leaving within the window owes nothing', 'after the window, only the extra time is charged, never the first part again', 'a second payment opens a new window from its own time'.

Alag 'paid until' state ki zaroorat nahi
Boundary tested
disadvantages: Monotonic pricing par depend karta hai
Window ek global option hai, per-customer nahi
common_mistakes: Window ke baad poora fee dobara charge karna (P6 jaisa)
Boundary off-by-one
Window entry time se ginna, payment time se nahi

question: A car stayed 25 hours with a daily cap of 8 hours and the customer disputes the bill. How do you explain it?
answer_hinglish:
Bill 9 ghante ka banta hai, 25 ka nahi. Rule: dailyCapHours ke saath har started 24 ghante (entry se gine, calendar day se nahi) mein maximum cap jitne ghante charge hote hain. 25 h = ek poora din (cap = 8) + 1 ghanta ka part-day = 8 + 1 = 9 hours. README isi example ko likhta hai. Car rate 5000 ho toh 45000.

Code: HourlyPricing.fee() pehle grace check karta hai (stay <= grace toh 0). Cap set hai toh `days = floor(stay / DAY_MS)`, `restHours = ceil((stay - days*DAY) / HOUR_MS)`, aur fee = (days x cap + min(restHours, cap)) x rate. Teen cheezein customer ko samjhaane layak: (1) har STARTED hour charge hota hai -- 1 ms bhi upar gaya toh agla ghanta; (2) grace ke upar gaye toh POORA stay charge hota hai, grace minus nahi hota (70 min with 10 min grace = 2 hours); (3) din entry time se ginta hai.

Tests exact cases dikhate hain: cap 8 par 7h+1ms = 8 hours, 24h = 8, 24h+1ms = 9, 24h+3h = 11, 2 din + 10h = 24. Mutations P17 (last part-day par cap nahi) 2 tests aur P18 (full days 24 h par) 2 tests se pakde gaye.

Dispute ke liye Receipt mein feeMinor, durationMs, exitAt aur payments list hai -- customer ko stay ka duration aur har payment dikha sakte ho. Lekin honest: lot exit ke baad koi history nahi rakhta (memory se entry delete), toh dispute ke liye receipt hi evidence hai jab tak persistence na ho.
why_needed: Pricing disputes support ka sabse common kaam hai. Rule ko ek line mein samjha pana aur tests se prove kar pana bharosa banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Mobile data pack: 'roz 1.5 GB tak charge, uske baad us din ka free' -- aur din recharge ke time se ginta hai, raat 12 baje se nahi.
how_it_works: Full days at cap + capped started hours of the last part-day. Fee non-decreasing hai stay ke saath (tested every 7 minutes over 3 days, with and without a cap).

Demo cap 8, grace 10, car 5000. src/parking-lot.ts Receipt { exitAt, durationMs, feeMinor, paidMinor, payments }.

Integer minor units -- rounding dispute nahi
Boundary cases tested

Exit ke baad lot mein history nahi -- receipt hi saboot

Hours round down karna

question: The provider charges the card but the response is lost on the network. Walk through what happens.
answer_hinglish:
Yahi failure ke liye idempotency key hai, aur is case mein customer ek hi baar charge hota hai aur lot record bhi kar leta hai.

Step by step (PayStation ke saath, ExitGate mein bhi same): beginPayment ticket lock karta hai, amount fix, paymentKey = naya UUID. chargeWithRetry pehla attempt bhejta hai. FakePaymentGateway ka 'lose-response' outcome: charge RECORD karta hai (byKey mein key -> charge), phir plain Error 'connection reset after the charge' phenkta hai. chargeWithRetry ke liye yeh decline nahi hai, toh 'unknown' -- 200 ms ruk kar (tests mein 0) dobara bhejta hai, SAME request object, same key. Ab gateway byKey mein key dhoondhta hai, mil jaati hai, amount aur reference same hain, toh naya charge nahi -- pehla paymentId lauta deta hai. chargeWithRetry woh id return karta hai, PayStation recordPayment karta hai.

Test 'lost response: the retry gets the same payment; charged once, recorded once' -- gateway.calls 2, totalChargedMinor 5000, paymentsFor length 1. payment.test.ts mein bhi: calls 2, charges 1, returned id == stored id. Demo bhi isi se shuru hota hai: pehla card answer lost, retry key reuse karta hai, ek charge.

Agar retry nayi key se hota (mutation P2), toh provider use naya payment samajhta: do charges, lot mein ek record -- customer ka double charge. P2 ne 7 tests fail kiye.

Edge: agar lost response AAKHRI attempt par ho, toh koi retry nahi bachta -- PAYMENT_UNKNOWN, aur paisa kat chuka hai. Woh alag (aur khatarnaak) case hai.
why_needed: Network par lost response sabse normal failure hai. Iska galat handling = double charge, jo sabse bura payment bug hai.
real_world_analogy: Aapne online order 'Pay' dabaya, page hang ho gaya. Dobara dabaya. Achhi website same order number se pehchaan leti hai ki payment ho chuka, dobara nahi kaatti.
how_it_works: At-least-once delivery + idempotent receiver = effectively-once effect. Key client generate karta hai, server key -> result store karta hai, repeat par stored result lautata hai.

Lot aur provider ke totals match
Fake gateway is failure ko deterministically reproduce karta hai
disadvantages: Provider ka idempotency support zaroori
Last-attempt lost response abhi bhi unresolved
common_mistakes: Lost response ko decline samajh lena
Retry par nayi key
Sochna ki timeout ka matlab 'charge nahi hua'

question: A car pays at the exit gate, then the barrier motor fails. What happens to the payment and to the next attempt?
answer_hinglish:
Payment recorded rehti hai, exit abort hota hai, car andar rehti hai, aur agla try kuch charge nahi karta.

ExitGate.leave(): beginExit (lock 'exiting', fee fix, key) -> due > 0 toh chargeWithRetry -> lot.recordPayment(ticketId, paymentId). Exit lock mein recordPayment lock ko khatam nahi karta, sirf `lock.dueMinor = 0` karta hai (pay station ka lock khatam hota hai, exit ka nahi). Phir withTimeout se device.open(). Barrier ne error phenka -> catch -> lot.abortExit(ticketId) -> DEVICE_FAILED ('the ticket is still valid').

abortExit() sirf status 'active' aur lock delete karta hai; entry.payments ko nahi chhoota. Comment: 'Payments recorded during the exit stay recorded: the next exit within the window owes nothing.' Agla beginExit bill() se nikaalta hai: aakhri payment ka `at` (jo exit lock ka time tha) window ke andar hai, toh price us time par, paid = fee, due 0. Gate charge hi nahi karta (`if (quote.dueMinor > 0)`), seedha barrier.

Test 'paid at the gate, then the barrier failed: the next try does not charge again': pehli koshish DEVICE_FAILED, paymentsFor length 1, 1 minute baad doosri koshish fee 5000 paid 5000, gateway.calls 1. Aur agar barrier ne error diya LEKIN sach mein khul gaya (driver ne signal ignore kiya), toh lot ke hisaab se car andar hai -- spot kabhi free nahi hoga. question: All three payment attempts fail without a clear answer (PAYMENT_UNKNOWN). Why is that not just 'failed', and what can still go wrong?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki 'mujhe jawab nahi mila' aur 'charge nahi hua' alag cheezein hain. Timeout, connection reset, 5xx -- in sab mein provider ne charge kar diya ho sakta hai. Isliye code decline ko hi final 'no' maanta hai (PaymentDeclinedError -> PAYMENT_DECLINED, retry nahi), aur baaki sab ko 'unknown': retry, aur aakhir mein PAYMENT_UNKNOWN, 'failed' nahi. PLAN.md: 'reported as unknown, not as failed, because it may have succeeded.'

PAYMENT_UNKNOWN par kya hota hai: PayStation abortPayment, ExitGate abortExit -- lock release, kuch record nahi, ticket active. Error ke `cause` mein last error hai (tested).

Ab khatarnaak hissa, jo code ko padh kar dikhta hai: agar teesra attempt 'lose-response' tha (ya teeno timeouts mein se kisi mein provider ne charge kar diya aur baad ke attempts bhi jawab na de paaye), toh paisa kat chuka hai lekin lot ke paas record nahi. Customer dobara pay karega -- naya beginPayment/beginExit, NAYI paymentKey (har lock ki apni key). Provider ke liye yeh naya payment hai: double charge. Purani key lock ke saath kho gayi.

Randomized test (invariants.test.ts) yeh case technically hit kar sakta hai (fail, fail, lose-response), lekin chosen 5 seeds mein provider total == lot total hota hai. Matlab invariant un seeds par proven hai, har possible run par nahi.

Fix jo built nahi: reconciliation -- unknown payment ki key aur amount persist karo, provider se poochho us key ka kya hua; charged mila toh lot mein record karo. README: 'finding out needs the provider's records (reconciliation), which is NOT built'.
why_needed: Unknown ko failed bolna = customer ko dobara pay karwana jab paisa shayad kat chuka. Yeh distributed systems ka classic 'in-doubt' case hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank transfer 'pending' dikha raha hai. Aap dobara bhej doge toh shayad do baar chala jaaye. Sahi kaam: bank se transaction id se status poochho.
how_it_works: Three outcomes: success (id mila), definite failure (decline), unknown (sab kuch aur). Unknown ko resolve karne ke liye idempotency key ke saath query ya same key se retry chahiye -- jo tabhi possible hai jab key yaad ho.
in_this_project: src/payment.ts chargeWithRetry(): `if (error instanceof PaymentDeclinedError) throw PAYMENT_DECLINED`, loop ke baad PAYMENT_UNKNOWN with cause. src/pay-station.ts catch -> abortPayment. src/parking-lot.ts lockEntry() har lock par naya randomUUID key. Tests: payment.test.ts 'transient failures are retried; all attempts failing is PAYMENT_UNKNOWN with the last cause'; money.test.ts 'outcome unknown: PAYMENT_UNKNOWN, ticket unlocked, nothing recorded'.

Decline par bekaar retry nahi (P3)
Cause chain debugging ke liye
disadvantages: Unknown ke baad key kho jaati hai -- agla try double charge kar sakta hai
Reconciliation nahi
common_mistakes: Unknown ko failed maan kar customer ko dobara charge karwana
Decline ko retry karna
Har error ko unknown maanna, decline ko bhi

Reconciliation job kaisa dikhega?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Last attempt lose-response: charged, unrecorded, ticket unlocked -> double charge on next pay. Provider down: sab unknown, koi charge nahi -- safe lekin reconciliation ko pata karna padega.
advanced.alternatives: Ticket par 'pending key' save karna aur agla lock usi key + amount ko reuse kare jab tak resolve na ho; ya unknown par lock ko 'needs-reconciliation' state mein rakhna; ya provider webhook se async result.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Unknowns rate ke saath reconciliation ka load badhta hai; batch mein provider report se match karna sasta.
advanced.production_improvements: Unknown payments ka durable queue, reconciliation job, customer ko 'pending check' receipt, double charge mile toh auto-refund (refund bhi built nahi).

question: How does the randomized test prove 'total charged by the provider == total recorded by the lot', and what are its limits?
answer_hinglish:
invariants.test.ts ke 'random concurrent gates' test mein 5 seeds (5-9), har ek mein 400 random steps: 3 entry gates, 2 exit gates jinke paas card reader hai. Devices ke calls pending rehte hain aur random order mein settle hote hain, 15% fail. Card reader ek wrapper hai jo har call par random outcome FakePaymentGateway mein enqueue karta hai: 75% approve, 10% decline, 8% lose-response, 7% fail.

Har step ke baad structural invariants check hote hain (spot states vs ticket statuses, har pending device call ke peeche claim). End mein teen money assertions: (1) receipts ki payments + andar khadi cars ki payments ka sum == fake.totalChargedMinor() -- koi double charge nahi, koi charge bina lot ke jaane nahi. (2) recorded payment ids unique. (3) har receipt mein paidMinor == feeMinor -- har nikalne wali car ne poora fee diya. Aur check hota hai ki run ne LOT_FULL, DEVICE_FAILED aur PAYMENT_DECLINED sab hit kiye, aur kuch receipts mein real payment hai -- taaki test 'kuch na hone' se pass na ho.

Yeh invariant kyun hold karta hai: har charge ki key ek lock ki hai; retries same key; lose-response ke baad koi bhi retry pehla payment lautata hai; recordPayment lock ka amount record karta hai (wahi gateway ko gaya); abortExit payments nahi hatata.

Limits jo main interview mein khud bolunga: (a) PRNG seeded hai -- yeh 5 specific runs ka proof hai, exhaustive nahi. (b) 'fail, fail, lose-response' sequence mathematically possible hai, aur tab charged-but-unrecorded hota (PAYMENT_UNKNOWN) -- invariant toot jaata; in seeds mein nahi hua. Yeh test ki kamzori nahi, design ka documented gap hai (reconciliation nahi). (c) Pay station is randomized test mein nahi hai, sirf exit gates. (d) 'hang' outcome nahi use hota. (e) Ek process, fake provider.
why_needed: Money bugs rare interleavings mein chhupte hain. Hand-written tests sirf woh cases pakadte hain jo aapne soche; randomized test unhe bhi jo nahi soche.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka end-of-day: har ATM ne jitna nikala aur ledger mein jitna likha, dono ka total milana. Ek ek transaction check karne ke bajaye totals se poori class ki galtiyan pakad lo.
how_it_works: Seeded PRNG (mulberry32) -> reproducible random schedule. Invariant checks after every step + global conservation check at the end. Coverage assertions (codes seen) taaki test vacuous na ho.
in_this_project: test/invariants.test.ts: rng(), checkInvariants(), 'random concurrent gates' describe, gateway wrapper with `fake.enqueue(r < 0.75 ? 'approve' : ...)`, end assertions `recorded.reduce(...) toBe(fake.totalChargedMinor())`. src/fake-gateway.ts totalChargedMinor(). README test table: invariants.test.ts (15 tests).
advantages: Conservation law ek line mein poori bug class pakadta hai
Seed se failure reproducible
Coverage assertion vacuous pass rokta hai
disadvantages: Sirf 5 seeds; rare sequences miss ho sakte hain
Pay station aur hang outcome covered nahi
Known gap (last-attempt lost response) test ke dayre mein aata hai lekin trigger nahi hota
common_mistakes: Random test ko proof maan lena
Unseeded randomness -- fail hua toh reproduce nahi
Sirf final state check karna, har step par nahi
follow_up_questions: Is test ko property-based testing library (fast-check) se kaise likhoge?
Last-attempt lost response ko deterministic test mein kaise dikhaoge?
Production mein yahi invariant kaise check hoga?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Seeded random tests sasti coverage dete hain aur reproducible hain; exhaustive model checking zyada strong hai magar mehnga. Fixed seeds CI ko stable rakhte hain magar naye interleavings nahi dhoondhte.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar test fail ho: seed test name mein hai, wahi run dobara. Ek known sequence (fail, fail, lose-response) invariant tod sakta hai -- yeh reconciliation ki zaroorat ka saboot hai.
advanced.alternatives: fast-check jaisa shrinking wala property testing; TLA+ se lock/payment protocol model check; nightly CI mein random seeds.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Steps aur seeds badhane se rare cases milte hain; CI time ke saath balance. Production mein same invariant reconciliation job ban jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Nightly run with random seeds aur failing seed log karna; pay station aur hang outcome ko bhi mix mein daalna; unknown payments ko 'pending' bucket mein gin ke invariant ko precise banana.

question: The pay-then-exit logic charges only the difference after the window. Why is that correct, and what pricing change would break it?
answer_hinglish:
Difference wala logic sahi hai kyunki pricing monotonic hai: lamba stay kabhi kam fee nahi deta. Window ke baad bill = fee(entry, now) - paid. paid pehle ki fee(entry, t_pay) thi, aur now > t_pay, toh fee(now) >= fee(t_pay), toh due >= 0 aur sirf extra time ka. Alag 'paid until' state rakhne ki zaroorat nahi -- PLAN.md isi ko simpler bata ke chunta hai.

Monotonicity tested hai: pricing.test.ts 'never charges less for a longer stay' teen configurations (cap 8; grace 10; grace 30 + cap 1) par 3 din tak har 7 minute par fee check karta hai ki pichli se kam na ho. Code mein Math.max(0, fee - paid) clamp bhi hai, comment kehta hai difference 'never negative (and is clamped to 0 anyway)'.

Kya tod dega: koi strategy jo lambe stay par kam fee de. Examples: 'pehle 3 ghante 50 per hour, 3 ghante se upar flat 100' -- 2.5 h = 150, 3.5 h = 100. Ya night flat rate jo din ke hourly se sasta ho. Tab: customer ne 2.5 h par 150 pay kiya, window ke baad 3.5 h par fee 100, due = max(0, 100-150) = 0. Clamp galat refund se bachata hai, lekin lot ab 'jitna fee utna paid' wali assumption kho deta hai -- receipt mein paidMinor > feeMinor ho sakta hai, jabki Receipt ka comment kehta hai paidMinor hamesha feeMinor ke barabar. Aur ulta case: pehle 'sasta' period mein pay kiya, baad mein mehnga hua -- difference theek chalega, kyunki woh sirf badhne par depend karta hai.

Interface PricingStrategy monotonicity enforce nahi karta; sirf checkedFee() non-negative integer check karta hai. Toh yeh ek implicit contract hai jo har nayi strategy ko test se prove karna chahiye.
why_needed: Pricing strategy pluggable hai (Strategy pattern); koi bhi nayi strategy likh sakta hai. Ek hidden assumption tootne par billing silently galat hogi.
real_world_analogy: Gym membership: 3 mahine pay kiye, phir 6 mahine ka plan liya toh sirf difference dete ho -- yeh tabhi chalta hai jab 6 mahine ka plan 3 mahine se sasta na ho.
how_it_works: Incremental billing correct hai iff f is non-decreasing in exit time. Proof: due = f(now) - f(t_pay) >= 0. Bina monotonicity ke incremental billing ko 'segments' mein price karna padega.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts bill() aur checkedFee(); src/pricing.ts comment 'The fee never goes down as the stay gets longer (the pay-then-exit window relies on that; tested)'. test/pricing.test.ts monotonic test. test/money.test.ts after-window test (15000 fee, 10000 paid, 5000 due). Mutation P6 (payments not subtracted) 12 tests fail.

Proof ek line ka
Clamp ek safety net
disadvantages: Implicit contract -- interface mein nahi likha
Non-monotonic tariffs support nahi
common_mistakes: Nayi strategy ke liye monotonic test na likhna
Clamp ko 'fix' samajh lena -- woh sirf symptom chhupata hai
Difference ki jagah poora fee dobara charge
follow_up_questions: Monotonicity ko lot runtime par check kar sakta hai kya?
Night flat rate chahiye toh billing kaise karoge?
Clamp hata dein toh kya fail hoga?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Non-monotonic strategy plug ki: overpayment silently, receipt paid > fee. Strategy fractional/negative de: checkedFee STRATEGY_BUG phenkta hai (yeh check hota hai).
advanced.alternatives: Paid-until timestamp + segments price karna (fee(t_pay, now) as separate stay); ya strategy interface mein 'incrementalFee(from, to)'.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale ka issue nahi, correctness ka hai; bahut saare tariffs/lots ho toh har strategy ke liye shared monotonicity property test.
advanced.production_improvements: PricingStrategy ke docs mein contract likhna, ek generic property test jo har registered strategy par chale, aur receipt par paid > fee ka alert.

question: Explain the payment architecture: why is payment modelled as a lock on the ticket, and how do PayStation, ExitGate and the booth share it?
answer_hinglish:
Payment ko lot ke andar ek aur lock ki tarah model kiya hai -- wahi shape jo stage 2 mein gates ke liye thi: synchronous lock, slow async kaam, phir synchronous record ya rollback. Teen jagah se paisa aata hai aur teeno ek hi primitive use karte hain.

PayStation.pay: lot.beginPayment() (ticket 'paying', amount fix, paymentKey) -> chargeWithRetry -> lot.recordPayment() (lock khatam, ticket active) ya failure par lot.abortPayment(). ExitGate.leave: lot.beginExit() (ticket 'exiting', fee fix, key) -> due ho toh charge + recordPayment (lock rehta hai, due 0) -> barrier -> commitExit; koi bhi failure -> abortExit. Booth exit(): beginExit -> cash recordPayment -> commitExit, sab synchronous.

Lock kyun: (1) concurrency -- do stations ya station + gate ek saath ek ticket par: doosre ko TICKET_BUSY, ek hi charge (tested: 'two stations with the same ticket at once: one charge'). Mutation P13 (lock nahi) 47 tests fail karta hai -- sabse bada number. (2) amount lock ke time fix -- slow card reader ke dauraan price nahi badalta, aur provider ko gaya amount == record hua amount. (3) idempotency key ka scope lock hai. (4) Lot methods synchronous hain, toh lock lena atomic hai -- JS ek synchronous block ke beech koi aur code nahi chalata.

Responsibilities: lot = rules aur state (kitna due, barrier rule, kaun lock rakhta hai). PayStation/ExitGate = orchestration aur I/O (provider, devices). PaymentGateway = provider boundary (sirf fake implement hai). Isliye naya payment channel (mobile app) sirf ek naya orchestrator hoga.

Limits: single process, in-memory; lock expiry nahi; reconciliation nahi; real provider nahi.
why_needed: LLD round ka follow-up 'payment fail ho toh?' yahi jaanchta hai ki aap money, concurrency aur failure ek saath design kar sakte ho, bina har gate mein logic copy kiye.
real_world_analogy: Bank locker: andar jaane se pehle register mein entry (lock), andar kaam (slow), bahar aakar sign-out (record) -- aur ek waqt mein ek hi aadmi us locker ke paas.
how_it_works: TicketStatus state machine: reserved -> active -> paying -> active (record/abort), active -> exiting -> (commitExit: gone) | active (abortExit). Lock object {kind, at, feeMinor, paidMinor, dueMinor, paymentKey}. Har transition ek synchronous lot method; async kaam sirf transitions ke beech.

Rules ek jagah, I/O alag

disadvantages: Single process par depend
Crash par lock atka (no expiry)
Lot ko payment concepts jaanne padte hain

advanced.failure_scenarios: Provider unknown: lock release, possible double charge later. Orchestrator crash: lock atka. Barrier fail after pay: payment rehti hai, retry free (tested).
advanced.alternatives: Payment ko alag service/aggregate banana jo lot ko 'paid' event bheje (eventual consistency); ya saga/workflow engine jo har step durable rakhe.
